data.body:
ADOPTED by a new session (the session that pushed Gerrit 2115 terminated unexpectedly). New evidence, confirmed independently against the CI API, explains why 2115 patchset 1 FAILED its own Verified run:

## Workflow provenance: the Verified gate runs trusted-main workflow files, not the patchset's

Change 2115 PS1 (a42a9d8d494) edited _build-and-test.yml --timeout=20 -> 300, but its Verified run 32587991195 carries headSha 6a5c88027c5 for workflow resolution (the 'classify Verify route from trusted main' job): the reusable workflows resolve at the CALLER's trusted-main sha. Job 97067339850 (pytest ubuntu py3.13) log line 989 shows the executed command was still `--timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread`. pytest-timeout precedence is CLI > INI, so main's stale --timeout=20 OVERRODE the patchset's ini timeout=300. Result: 13x 'node down: Not properly terminated', 26x "worker 'gwN' crashed", 0x 'Failed: Timeout' — the identical signature. The fix was never actually exercised by its own gate; a config-only restore CAN NEVER pass while main's workflow carries the tighter CLI flag.

## The mechanism that closes the loophole: MARKER > CLI > INI, verified empirically

pytest-timeout's _get_item_settings (pytest_timeout.py:388) takes marker values first; CLI/env/ini only fill unset fields. Verified by local experiment (worktree venv, pytest-timeout installed):
- ARM 1: @pytest.mark.timeout(60) test sleeping 5s under hostile --timeout=2 --timeout-method=thread -> 1 passed in 5.01s (marker beats CLI).
- ARM 2 (control): same test UNMARKED, same CLI -> Timeout at 2s.
- ARM 3: marker applied by a conftest pytest_collection_modifyitems hook from ini timeout=60, hostile --timeout=2 -> 1 passed in 5.04s.
- ARM 4: same under -n 2 --dist worksteal -> 2 passed, zero node-downs.
- ARM 5 (guard intact): hook active, ini=2, NO CLI, unmarked 5s test -> Timeout at 2s.

So the fix gains a conftest hook that applies the ini budget as a timeout marker to unmarked items, making the repo's ini authoritative even under a stale CLI flag — exactly the transition run's situation.

## Why a FLOOR, not a blanket marker

A blanket marker at ini=300 would silently LOWER the live lanes' deliberately larger CLI budgets (external-integration 900/600/1800, structured-output 3600, test.yml 600, _optionality 600), because marker > CLI. The hook therefore fires only when the effective non-marker budget (CLI > PYTEST_TIMEOUT env > ini, pytest-timeout's own resolution order) is positive and BELOW the ini budget: a stale tighter flag cannot undercut the ini, a deliberately looser lane budget still wins, and --timeout=0 (explicit disable, e.g. for debugging) is respected.

## Secondary symptom, now explained (follow-up to be filed)

When a worker dies mid-test under the integration tier's --dist loadgroup, the run HANGS until the job-level ~60-min cap (job 97060825848 hung 40+ min). Worker death is the trigger; the hang is amplification — a resilience defect independent of the budget, to be filed as its own ticket linked discovered_from this one.

Plan/description being updated to the conftest-floor shape; file_impact to be declared; review-plan to be re-run before the amended patchset is pushed.
